%%R -i x -o y

What would be the best way to do this without relying on magics?

Thanks in advance,
-Alessandro

messages.subject: Re: [Rpy] load nnet in rpy2
messages.body_plain:
Ah, yes. Good you did. The licensing had all the attention.

The following is completely untested, but should get you going (and with 
some luck, just work as it is)

from rpy2.robjects.packages import importr
base = importr('base')
nnet = importr('nnet')
# load: the side effect is to populate the R global environment
# with whatever in the file. I am assuming that 'err_net' comes from it.
base.load('err_net.RData')
from rpy2.robjects import globalenv
err_net = globalenv['err_net']
y = nnet.predict(err_net, x)

messages.body_plain:
On 12/02/2013 07:36 PM, Alessandro Gagliardi wrote:
> Thanks! That got me there, with only the following minor adjustments 
> (recorded for posterity):
>
> First, it's nnet.predict_nnet()(not nnet.predict())

Ah, yes. The so-called S3 dispatch in R. The generic for predict() is in 
"stats". What you have is perfectly fine. The alternative would have been:

stats = importr('stats')
stats.predict(err_net, x)


>
> Also, I had to convert my pandas DataFrame to an R data.frame this way:
>
> import pandas.rpy.common as com
> r_df = com.convert_to_r_dataframe(pd_df)

With rpy2-2.4.0-dev, the conversion can be made automagic:

from rpy2.robjects import pandas2ri
pandas2ri.activate()
# from now on, a pandas DataFrame passed to an R function will be 
converted on-the-fly


>
> -Alessandro

messages.subject_clean: [Rpy] rpy2 (v.2.3.8) fails to load on Windows 7
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am attempting to use rpy2 within the IPython Notebook (v 1.1), and I am
having difficulty getting to to work.  The mail list seems to suggest that
rpy v2.3.8 was written specifically to work with R v3.0.2, but when I
attempt to run any rpy2 code, I get the following error:

"Unable to locate R.dll within C:\Program Files\R\R-3.0.2\bin\R.exe"

I know getting rpy2 to work on 64-bit Windows 7 machines has been
difficult, but if anyone has figured it out, I would be quite grateful.
 After making sure that everything is up to date and looking through the
mail-list archives, I am not at all sure how to proceed.

Thanks,
